children: Shares of Paytm and One Mobikwik rose in opening trade on Wednesday, a day after the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) announced a new merchant discount rate (MDR) framework for select UPI transactions.
Stocks of One 97 Communications, the parent company of Paytm, rose 4.62% to Rs 1,810, while One Mobikwik Systems gained 4.71% to Rs 210.32 as of 9:16 am on Wednesday.

Under the new framework, an MDR of up to 0.4% will apply to person-to-merchant (P2M) UPI transactions above Rs 2,000 from October 15, with concessional rates for select categories and exemptions for small merchants. Transactions up to Rs 2,000, which account for more than 95% of P2M volume, will remain at zero MDR, while P2P transfers will continue to remain free.
Paytm on Tuesday said the new MDR framework would generate additional revenue from its merchant business.
"This will generate additional revenue from the merchant business for many of the payment transactions that were free earlier," the company said in a regulatory filing.
"As per the NPCI Circular, no charge is levied on customers for UPI payments, which shall continue to remain free of charge for them," Paytm added. Here’s what brokerages are saying:
JM Financial said the 40 bps MDR was materially higher than the 25 bps it had modelled earlier, although broader exemptions prompted it to cut its eligible GMV assumption to 20% from 30%.
"Retaining our 20% share assumption for Paytm, pass-through rises to 8bps (from 5bps)," JM Financial said.
The brokerage estimates incremental revenue of Rs 2.1 billion in FY27 and Rs 4.7 billion in FY28 for Paytm, with incremental adjusted EBITDA of Rs 1.4 billion and Rs 4.4 billion, respectively.

JM Financial reiterated its 'Buy' rating and raised its target price to Rs 2,150 from Rs 1,950. "The NPCI is yet to specify how the MDR pool shall be distributed across the value chain," it said, calling the allocation a major risk factor.
Citi said the framework marks a shift away from the zero-MDR regime for larger merchant payments.
"An MDR of 0.4% (capped at Rs 300) applies to transactions above Rs 2,000," Citi said, while noting that roughly 96% of P2M volumes would remain free.
The brokerage estimates the banking ecosystem could gain Rs 16,000-17,000 crore annually in new revenue, with Yes Bank seeing an estimated 6-12% boost to PBT.
JPMorgan said the framework represents a "shift from zero-MDR regime to transaction-linked revenue model for banks, PSPs & UPI apps".

It said acquiring banks can charge large merchants 40 bps on P2M transactions above Rs 2,000, capped at Rs 300, while small P2PM merchants receiving up to Rs 1 lakh a month through UPI QR remain exempt.
JPMorgan added that consumers remain protected, with no UPI payment charges and apps barred from imposing platform fees.

title: Paytm, One Mobikwik shares jump up to 5% after UPI MDR announcement; brokerages see revenue boost
